# Sample EQ Reference Vectors

The 50 vectors contain three existing Sample payload regression values and
47 additional vectors read from a sampler-saved image after explicit EQ edits.
They are stored signed Q13 coefficients in `b1,b2,b0,-a1,-a2` order, not values
generated by the tests. Both native and Python tests consume this file without
requiring the source image.

The original neutral and high-shelf cases still require byte-exact output.
Frequency 27 and the additional saved vectors permit one Q13 unit per
coefficient, reflecting final quantization. This tolerance applies to
regeneration only; preservation always requires exact bytes.

## Sampler-Save References

Rows with `source: sampler-save-00114` retain the Sample identity in
`source_sample`. Source image SHA-256:
`13134a508ca258c4860d1330fd1cba5cd53ff9e8ca460ef87de758db083abc65`.
The exact device model and software revision were not recorded; these vectors
are regression references for the saved parameter tuples, not a model-specific
compatibility certification.

Coverage includes low/high shelf boost and cut, both sides of all six high-shelf
gain-clamp thresholds, frequency endpoints, neutral settings, and Peak/Dip Width.
Shelf Width is stored but does not affect the shelf response. Test inputs use
the saved values, not the settings suggested by a Sample name: `L37+06W120`
was saved at +4 dB and is labeled accordingly. It is not a +6 dB reference.

Native tests cover fresh Samples, Sample Bank parameter state, member overrides,
and explicit edits to each EQ field. Python tests cover coefficient generation
and Sample serialization. Both test byte-exact preservation of saved and
deliberately divergent vectors during unrelated edits, followed by regeneration
when an EQ field is explicitly supplied, even if its semantic value is unchanged.
